newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch-led engineering group wins big gas contract.
newsitem.headline: Dutch-led engineering group wins big gas contract.

text.p: A three-nation consortium headed by Dutch engineering group Stork has won a one-billion guilder ($594.2 million) contract to upgrade gas installations in the Netherlands' largest gas field, Stork said on Wednesday.

The contract, awarded by Royal Dutch/Shell-Exxon joint venture Nederlandse Aardolie Maatschappij (NAM), involves renovating, installing compressors and maintaining 11 of NAM's 29 production facilities in the massive northern Dutch Slochteren field.

"We are overjoyed at having won this unique commission," said Peter Boerma of Stork unit Delaval-Stork and spokesman for the Stork GLT consortium, which also includes Siemens of Germany and Japanese industrial instruments maker Yokogawa.
Boerma said the definitive contract, due to be signed next February, would also include an option for the consortium to take on the renovation of the other 18 production facilities.
NAM said in a statement that the total cost of upgrading all 29 installations amounted to around three billion guilders, requiring an estimated 10,000 man-years of work.
"The renovations will safeguard the key role of the Slochteren gas field in Dutch gas policy over the coming decades," NAM said.
A vital element of the renovation project is the installation of compressors at each facility to cope with the reductions in pressure throughout the field.
"The Stork units will together be responsible for the design, construction and supply of the compressors," Boerma said. This represented around 70 percent of the project, he added.
Siemens, which will supply the engines to drive the compressors, has a 20 percent interest in the consortium, while Yokogawa has 10 percent, Boerma said.
The first upgraded installation is due for delivery by winter 1998/99, with the remaining 10 to follow by 2005.
"When this first phase is completed a decision will be taken on renovation of the remaining installations," Boerma said.
The contract also involves maintenance of the upgraded installations, for an estimated 25-year period, he added.
Stork shares leapt on the news, gaining 2.60 guilders or 4.68 percent to 58.20 guilders on a lower Amsterdam bourse.
Earlier this year the industrial group acquired the profitable maintenance activities of bankrupt Dutch planemaker Fokker. ($1=1.683 Guilder)
